questions.question:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the* sings and to balance the given equation.

25 * 5 * 10 * 2 * 4 * 3
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

By using BODMAS (Brackets of division, multiplication, addition and subtraction) and going by the options,

**Option (1) -, +, ÷, ×, =**

Given equation: 25 * 5 * 10 * 2 * 4 * 3

Putting the signs: 25 - 5 + **10 ÷ 2** × 4 = 3

25 - 5 + **5 × 4** = 3

**25** - 5 **+ 20** = 3

45 - 5 = 3

40 = 3

LHS ≠ RHS

**Option (2) ×, ÷, -, +, =**

Given equation: 25 * 5 * 10 * 2 * 4 * 3

Putting the signs: 25 × **5 ÷ 10** - 2 + 4 = 3

**25 × 0.5** - 2 + 4 = 3

**12.5 + 2** = 3

14.5 = 3

LHS ≠ RHS

**Option (3) ÷, ×, +, -, =**

Given equation: 25 * 5 * 10 * 2 * 4 * 3

Putting the signs: **25 ÷ 5** × 10 + 2 - 4 = 3

**5 × 10** + 2 - 4 = 3

**52 - 4** = 3

48 = 3

LHS ≠ RHS

**Option (4) ÷, -, +, ×, =**

Given equation: 25 * 5 * 10 * 2 * 4 * 3

Putting the signs: **25 ÷ 5** - 10 + 2 × 4 = 3

5 - 10 + **2 × 4 **= 3

**5** - 10 + **8** = 3

**13 - 10** = 3

3 = 3

LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is** option (4).**

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III, Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All apples are bananas. 

All grapes are bananas.

All bananas are nuts.

**Conclusion:**

I. All apples are nuts.

II. All grapes are nuts.

III. No nuts are bananas.

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows-

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6265e47958f70e7addc0ce3f1e694851d2b13ccc1c66da35be1c4e90bdddeefd.png] 

Conclusion:

I. All apples are nuts. → True (as all apples are bananas and all bananas are nuts)

II. All grapes are nuts. → True (as all grapes are bananas and all bananas are nuts)

III. No nuts are bananas. → False (as all bananas are nuts; some nuts will definitely be bananas)

Hence, only conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

questions.question: If 26 January 2019 was Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 30 January 2022?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

i) In any two consecutive ordinary years, date of the next year will be one day ahead of the same day in the previous year.

ii) And** if a leap year** comes immediately after an ordinary year, then the day on a certain date of leap year will

(1)** 1 day ahead** of the same day of the ordinary year **upto February**,

(2)** 2 days ahead** of the same day of the ordinary year from** March to December**.

Therefore,

26 January 2019 = **Saturday**

26 January 2020 = **Sunday **

26 January 2021 = **Tuesday**

26 January 2022 =** Wednesday**

From 26 January to 30 January 2022

30 - 26 = 4 days 

**4 days after Wednesday is Sunday**

Hence, the correct answer is** Sunday.**
